newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sector Capital, Privatbank in Ukrainian venture.
newsitem.headline: Sector Capital, Privatbank in Ukrainian venture.

text.p: Moscow investment bank Sector Capital said on Thursday it was forming an asset management company with Ukraine's biggest bank, Privatbank, to attract Western funds to Ukrainian markets and privatised companies.
The two partners will hold equal shares in the new company, Sector Capital said in a statement.

Sector plans to launch a $200 million Russia-Ukraine fund this autumn. Sector Asset Management will manage the Russian allocation and the new company will manage the Ukrainian allocation, expected to be 40 percent of the total.

"Ukraine is on a verge of establishing its privatisation programme and has already attracted significant interest by global investors," the statement quoted Sector Capital President Jack Barbanel as saying. "Ukraine is where Russia was two to three years ago.
"We jointly believe that Ukraine presents enormous opportunities for global investors."
Privatbank Chairman Gennady Bogolubov said the venture expected support from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and other multilateral agencies.
"Ukraine has vast investment potential and Privatbank is uniquely qualified to assist in private equity deal flow and sourcing appropriate equity investment opportunities," he said.
Bogolubov took over as chairman recently following the appointment of his predecessor, Serhiy Tyhypko, as deputy prime minister in charge of the economy.

Sector Capital is owned by British fund manager Capital Group's New Europe East Investment Fund, the EBRD, Austrian investment bank European Privatisation and Investment Corp (EPIC), the Czech Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. and Germany electrical engineering group Siemens AG.
